summary: Trịnh Xuân Thuận is a scholar in religious studies and other fields. He studied at the California Institute of Technology (~1967–1969) and Princeton University (~1969–1974), and took up a post at the University of Virginia around 1976.

Tse-fu Kuan works in Buddhist studies. He completed a doctoral thesis at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich in 2004, held a postdoctoral post at National Cheng Kung University, and was affiliated with Yuan Ze University (attested 2015).

Tsenshab Serkong Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Ganden Monastery, earning the Geshe Lharampa degree. He held a post at Ganden Jangtse Monastery and taught Tenzin Gyatso, Alexander Berzin, and Thubten Chodron.

Tsering Dhundup Gonkatsang works in Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Panjab University, Tibetan Children's Village, and the University of Glasgow (1987). He served as headmaster at Tibetan Children's Village and became an Instructor in Tibetan at Oxford in 2001.
Tsering Gyaltsen is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and under the traditional teacher Dudjom Rinpoche.

Tsering Shakya is a Tibetology and history scholar. He earned his BA, MPhil, and PhD from SOAS, where he was a research fellow (1999–2002). He taught at Oxford and joined the University of British Columbia as a Research Chair (~2005).
Tsewang Gyurme is a scholar in Tibetology and history. He served as president of the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences and as president of the Tibetan Association for Sacred Studies (attested 2006).

Tsikey Chokling Rinpoche worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Young Lamas Home School, served as master of Vajrayana ceremonies at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling (~1976–2020), and was a board member of Rangjung Yeshe Shenpen.

Tsoknyi Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Khampagar Monastery and under teachers including Khamtrul Rinpoche Dongyud Nyima, Nyoshul Khenpo, Dilgo Khyentse, Tulku Urgyen, and Adeu Rinpoche. He held a post at Tergar Osel Ling.

Tsuguhito Takeuchi was a linguist and Tibetologist. He studied at Kyoto University, the University of Pennsylvania, and Indiana University (PhD, 1994) under Christopher I. Beckwith and Tatsuo Nishida, later serving as Professor of Linguistics at Kobe City University (~1998–2017).

Tsugunari Kubo worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at the University of Tokyo and Rissho University. He served as president of Reiyukai (~1975–1993; ~1996–2013) and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (~1987–2004), which he founded in 1982.
Tsui Lan Liza Cheung is a scholar in Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Hong Kong, earning a PhD under K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2013), and also studied under Toshiichi Endo.

Tsukasa Mizushima is an Indology and history scholar. Educated at the University of Tokyo, he held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1979–1995), served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1997–2018), and taught at the Open University of Japan (~2014–2021).

Tsultrim Allione works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at Antioch University and under teachers including the 16th Karmapa, Chögyam Trungpa, Kalu Rinpoche, Apho Rinpoche, Abo Rinpoche, and Namkhai Norbu. She founded Tara Mandala in 1993.

Tsultrim Gyatso is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He served as a senior instructor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and as abbot of Drepung Gomang Dratsang (attested 1987).

Tsultrim Kelsang is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He held teaching posts at Otani University as lecturer (attested 1984) and professor (attested 1999–2002), and was a guest researcher at Ryukoku University in 2015.

Tsuneki Nishiwaki works in philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Tokyo University of Education (~1963–1967), he held posts at Doshisha University (~1974–1984) and served as a professor at Kyoto University (~1993–2007).

Tsuruji Sahoda was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University (~1922–1925) and subsequently held academic posts at Osaka University (~1950–1963) and Ritsumeikan University (~1963–1972).
Tsutomu Hatai was an Indology scholar who served as president of the Ayurveda Research Society, where he succeeded Hiroshi Maruyama (attested 1987).
Tsutomu Horio is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under Keiji Nishitani and served as a professor at Otani University (attested 1990).
